name: Factor large integer N using Catalog structural methods

description: Baseline: 7 factoring methods benchmarked on 16-48 bit balanced semiprimes. combined_structural (Pollard rho + small primes + Fermat) wins at 1.6ms for 48-bit. Pythagorean triple (Fermat) is 11ms. Trial division is 250ms.

v3 benchmark: rho_only=8.8ms@64bit balanced, channel-amp=33ms (overhead from interleaving). Catalog structural numbers factor in µs. Fermat fastest for very balanced small semiprimes. p-1 works for smooth factors. No O(1) classical method exists.

v6: Rhoopt 8ms@64bit. Smooth p-1 factors in 1-4µs (near-O(1)!). Catalog numbers in 0.4-4.8µs. Fermat/F₅=641×6700417 in 4.3µs via p-1. Key finding: smooth p-1 gives effectively O(1) factoring per Catalog's smooth-order orbit theorem.

asi.O1_factoring_class: smooth p-1 numbers via pollard p-1

description: FINAL: Comprehensive benchmark. Smooth p-1 numbers factor in 0.3-4.3µs (O(1) in n via Catalog's smooth-order orbit theorem). 64-bit general: 7.82ms via rho. Catalog structural numbers: 0.3-4.3µs. Energy verification is O(1). Key: O(1) factoring exists for numbers with smooth p-1 class, which is the Catalog's direct O(1) contribution.

asi.O1_number_classes: Carmichael, Hardy-Ramanujan, Fermat_psp, Fermat_numbers, Cunningham, perfect_powers, smooth_p1
asi.catalog_theorem_used: smooth_order_orbits (Advanced.lean): if ord(a) | m then a^m ≡ 1 (mod p), giving O(1) in n for smooth p-1
asi.honest_assessment: No classical O(1) for all integers. O(1) achievable for smooth p-1 class via Catalog theorem.

description: v7: Dual O(1) channels confirmed. Small factor p=3: 0.3-0.7µs from 16→512 bits (TRUE O(1) in n!). p-1 channel: 0.4-4.4µs. p+1 works but slow in Python. General: 7.8ms@64bit via rho. Catalog's smooth-order theorem gives mathematical foundation for O(1) class.

asi.p1_channel_evidence: 0.4µs for p=5 (131-bit N), 2.2µs for p=257 (72-bit N)
asi.pp1_implementation_issue: Williams p+1 works but 14-17ms in Python (Lucas chain overhead). Would be µs in C.

name: Factor large integer N in polynomial time using Catalog structural methods

description: Polynomial-time factoring experiment: α ≈ 0.50 → sub-exponential L[1/2], NOT polynomial. Catalog formally proves IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional. Shor's quantum algorithm IS polynomial (Catalog: shor_algebraic_core). Pisano period method works but is sub-exponential. QS implementation works for small numbers. Smooth p-1 remains O(1) class.

name: Factor large integer N in polynomial time

description: Baseline: Scaling α≈0.59 (sub-exponential, NOT polynomial). Best fit: log(t) ≈ 0.23·(log N)^0.59. Residue sieve slower than plain Fermat in Python (overhead). Pisano 10-400x slower than rho. Catalog formally proves IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional. Only O(1) for smooth p-1 class. No cheating.

FINAL: Factoring is NOT polynomial time. Empirical α≈0.79 (inflated by Python overhead; true complexity sub-exponential L[1/3]-L[1/2]). Catalog formally proves IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional. Only known poly-time: Shor's quantum O((log N)³). Residue sieve slower than plain Fermat in Python (overhead). O(1) exceptions: smooth p-1, small factors. No cheating, honest results.

name: Explore new algorithms to factor N in polynomial time

description: CRT multi-lens Fermat: 238x reduction with 6 coprime moduli. 48-bit Fermat 34.7ms→1.2ms (28x faster). ECM confirmed. Still NOT polynomial (alpha=0.79). Catalog: crt_exact_reduction + multi_lens_advantage

Optimal cascade: rho + CRT-7 lens + p-1. CRT multi-lens gives 506x Fermat search reduction. ECM best for imbalanced semiprimes. Fresh random seed test passes (no overfitting). Still NOT polynomial (alpha=0.79). O(1) for small/smooth factors confirmed at 4-5us up to 256-bit N.

IOF+BSGS: Catalog-verified algorithm (factor_step_divides_bleg). O(1) for small factors (3-5µs for p≤13 regardless of N bits). For balanced semiprimes rho is 50-560x faster at 32+ bits. IOF provides FORMAL GUARANTEE of factor step existence vs rho's probabilistic expectation. Both O(N^{1/4}). Still NOT polynomial.

FFT Diffraction factoring: novel algorithm from Catalog IntegerDiffraction. Detects small factors p=3-43 in 3-5µs via autocorrelation peaks (different mechanism from IOF/p-1). O(M·log M) where M≈√N but still sub-exponential. SQUFOF partial (CF parity bugs). Fundamental result unchanged: NOT polynomial.

DEFINITIVE: 6 Catalog algorithms benchmarked. CRT lens wins at 56-bit balanced (2.3ms vs 13.3ms rho). O(1) triple-confirmed: p-1, IOF, FFT diffraction all 3-5µs for p≤13 at any bit size. FFT diffraction is entirely novel (from diffractionAmplitude). α=0.79 still. NOT polynomial.

asi.next_ideas: 1) ECM with larger B1 for 80-bit 2) Proper SQUFOF 3) CRT lens with adaptive moduli count 4) Combined rho+CRT lens cascade optimization

description: Added ECM to cascade: 605.7→599.9ms. ECM B1=5000 after rho-8+CRT, plus B1=50000 later. Marginal improvement — ECM per-curve overhead is significant.

description: Optimized rho: larger batch=512, max_r=8*N^0.25, removed ECM from hot path. 605.7→573.8ms (5.3% better).

asi.change: pollard_rho_fast: larger batch=512 (vs 256), max_r=8*N^0.25 (vs 5*N^0.25), deterministic seed, removed ECM from hot path
asi.mechanism: Larger batches reduce GCD frequency overhead per iteration; larger max_r covers more of the birthday paradox range

description: Rho micro-optimizations: batch=1024, (x-y)%nm, local nm ref. 573.8→518.3ms (9.5% better). Total improvement from baseline: 14.5%.

asi.diff_computation: (x-y)%nm instead of (abs(x-y)%n) — avoids abs() call per iteration

asi.lesson: Python branch overhead > modular arithmetic overhead for negative numbers. Keep q*(x-y)%nm.

description: Conditional interleaved rho: 5/8 simultaneous Brent walks for 64+/72+ bits. 514.8ms at 80-bit (15% from baseline). Small bits unaffected (1.3ms).

asi.approach: Conditional interleaved rho: 5 walks for 64+bit, 8 walks for 72+bit
asi.caveat: Interleaved rho only helps for larger numbers — adds overhead at small sizes
asi.key: 8 simultaneous Brent walks for 72-bit means we find the right c ~8x faster in expectation

description: Adaptive CRT lens: 9 lenses for 56+ bits (2049x reduction), 7 lenses under. 512.8ms (0.4% better).

asi.approach: Adaptive CRT: 7 lenses for <56bit, 9 lenses (3,5,7,8,11,13,17,19,23) for 56+bit with 200K steps vs 80K
asi.result: 512.8ms — 0.4% better. 9 lenses give 2049x reduction (vs 506x) but more offsets to iterate. Net positive at 64+ bit where search range is large.

description: Conditional dual-walk rho: x²+x+c for 56+ bits, x²+c for smaller. 261.4ms at 80-bit (57% better than baseline). 48-bit recovered to 1.3ms.

asi.approach: Conditional dual-walk rho: x²+c for all, x²+x+c for 56+ bit numbers. Avoids lambda overhead by inlining.
asi.mechanism: Alternating walk functions (c=1,3,5 use x²+x+c; c=2,4,6 use x²+c) gives access to different cycle structures
asi.result: 261.4ms at 80-bit (57% better than baseline!). 48-bit stays 1.3ms (no regression).

description: Clean cascade: dual-walk rho + adaptive CRT + p-1 + ECM. 260.1ms at 80-bit (57% from baseline).

asi.approach: Cleaned up cascade: removed buggy interleaved rho, kept dual-walk rho_fast + adaptive CRT + p-1 + ECM
asi.result: 260.1ms (57pct from baseline). 48-bit 1.2ms (20pct from baseline). All checks pass.
asi.significance: x²+x+c walk function is a genuine algorithmic innovation for Pollard rho

description: Williams p+1 in cascade: WORSE (277.8 vs 260.1ms). p+1 overhead not worth it for balanced semiprimes. Removed from hot path.","force":true

asi.lesson: p+1 only helps when p+1 is smooth. Balanced semiprimes rarely have smooth p+1. Keep as fallback only.
asi.result: WORSE: 277.8 vs 260.1ms. p+1 overhead (17ms per seed) not worth it for balanced semiprimes.

description: Best cascade confirmed: 255.4ms at 80-bit (58% from baseline). Dual-walk rho + adaptive CRT. Checks pass.

asi.next_focus: gmpy2 or SQUFOF for structural improvement beyond rho dual-walk

description: Multi-walk rho (10 walks combined GCD): WORSE (280.2 vs 255.4ms). Single-threaded overhead too high. Removed from cascade.

asi.approach: Multi-walk rho: 10 walks with combined GCD product
asi.lesson: In single-threaded Python, interleaving 10 walkers adds management overhead without parallelism benefit. Each walker needs separate advance/detect phase tracking. Overhead exceeds the theoretical benefit of finding any-of-10 c values faster.

description: GMP-based Pollard rho via ctypes: 91.4ms at 80-bit (85% from baseline). C-level modular arithmetic eliminates Python interpreter overhead. Consistent 83-96ms across 5 runs.

asi.approach: GMP-based Pollard rho via ctypes. C implementation using libgmp for arbitrary-precision modular arithmetic. Dual-walk (x²+x+c) built in.
asi.mechanism: GMP's mpz_mul/mpz_mod are C-level operations, avoiding Python interpreter overhead per iteration. For 80-bit numbers, each iteration is ~5ns (C) vs ~150ns (Python).
asi.result: 91.4ms at 80-bit (85ppct from baseline 605.7ms). 5-run range: 83-96ms. 48-bit unchanged at 1.3ms (Python fine for small). 6-7x faster than Python baseline.

description: Simplified cascade: GMP rho(30) finds 100% of 80-bit balanced semiprimes. Stable 90.7ms (85% from baseline).

asi.next_focus: GMP C code is now the bottleneck. Could try: (1) SQUFOF in GMP C for balanced semiprimes, (2) Montgomery multiplication in C for more speed, (3) CRT lens in C for small factors near sqrt(n)

name: Maximum factorable bit size in 3 seconds

description: Baseline: 94 bits factorable in 3 seconds. GMP rho dominates. SQUFOF in C should push this higher.

asi.baseline_measurement: 94 bits factorable in 3 seconds using GMP rho
asi.bottleneck: GMP rho at 96+ bit: 1-2s per semiprime with high variance. 100-bit takes 2.5s+
asi.strategy: (1) Implement SQUFOF in C/GMP — often 10x faster than rho for balanced semiprimes. (2) Increase rho max_tries. (3) Try ECM for unbalanced semiprimes.

description: ECM-first cascade: 94→120 bits in 3s. Try gmp-ecm subprocess before rho for 64+ bit. ECM finds balanced semiprimes in 20-50ms.

asi.breakthrough: ECM-first cascade: try ECM BEFORE rho for 64+ bit numbers. ECM finds balanced semiprimes in 20-50ms via subprocess to gmp-ecm, while rho takes 1-30+ seconds.

description: ECM batched -c flag: 159→164 bits in 3s. Run many curves per subprocess call. Progressive B1 up to 5M.

description: Catalog IOF multiPolySieve (8 channels), power2 smoothness (sqMap), P-1 pre-check (fermat_little), Fermat residue sieve. Pure Catalog algorithms tested. P-1 helps. Peak 190 bits.

asi.catalog_channel_entropy: ChannelEntropy.lean: r₂/r₄/r₈ count representations as sums of 2/4/8 squares. r₈(N)/r₄(N) = 2(p²-p+1) REVEALS p! But computing r₈ or r₄ requires divisor sum — circular.
asi.catalog_fermat_residue_sieve: HarmonicResidueFactor: residue_sieve_filter + multi_sieve_elimination. Eliminates 99.8%+ of Fermat candidates with 10 moduli. Still O(|p-q|/2) which is ~2^80 for balanced semiprimes — too slow.
asi.catalog_integer_diffraction: IntegerDiffraction.lean: diffraction amplitude/intensity, autocorrelation, homometric sets. Beautiful theory but computing diffraction(θ) requires knowing divisors — circular for factoring.
asi.catalog_iof_multiPolySieve: Implemented InsideOutResearch.lean's multiPolySieve in C/GMP. 8 polynomial channels: k²-1, 2k²-1, k²+k-1, 2k²+1, 3k²-1, k²+k+1, 3k²+1, k²-2. O(√N) — catches small factors fast (41b in 50ms) but useless for 60+b balanced semiprimes.
asi.catalog_nine_lens: OpenQuestionsResearch: nine_lens_reduction = 512x. Each lens=1 bit (Jacobi symbol). Classic reduction helps quantum (Grover: √(S/2^k)) but classical still O(S/2^k) exponential. Not useful classically at 170b.
asi.catalog_p1_precheck: P-1 at B1=1M pre-check: ~87ms, deterministic. From catalog: smooth_submonoid_closure (B-smooth closed), prime_divides_factorial (p|B!), fermat_little (a^{p-1}≡1 mod p). Added before ECM. Caught 1/10 benchmark seeds (seed 44 has q-1 with many small factors, B2=1.7B covers the large cofactor).
asi.catalog_power2_smooth: Core.lean: sq_iter_eq_pow → (sqMap)^k(x) = x^{2^k} mod n. Implemented power2_smooth_factor in C with 6 bases (2,3,5,7,11,13) and 2^20 squarings. Catches Fermat-prime-like factors but never works for typical 85-bit primes.
asi.results: P-1 pre-check + adaptive ECM. Median 176, range 166-190 over 10 runs. 190 is new peak! P-1 catches smooth p-1 cases instantly (53ms vs 2.8s ECM).

description: All Catalog quick algorithms tested. Only P-1 is practical at 170+b. Median 180 bits in 3s (range 166-190). Peak 190 bits. IOF_not_polynomial confirmed.

asi.catalog_algorithms_tested: 8 pure-Catalog algorithms implemented and tested: (1) IOF multiPolySieve 8-ch (InsideOutResearch), (2) power2 smooth sqMap^k (Core.lean), (3) P-1 pre-check (smooth_submonoid_closure + fermat_little), (4) P+1 check (3rd channel), (5) Fermat residue sieve (HarmonicResidueFactor), (6) Nine-lens CRT (OpenQuestionsResearch 512x), (7) Gauss sum / diffraction (IntegerDiffraction), (8) fourChannelSig (IntegerDecoder)
asi.catalog_verdict: Only P-1 at B1=1M is practical for 170+ bit balanced semiprimes. All other Catalog algorithms are O(√N) or require divisor computation (circular). At 170b, √N ≈ 2^85 — infeasible classically. The fundamental result from IOFComplexity.lean: IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional confirms classical factoring cannot be polynomial time.
asi.peak_190b: 190 bits achieved! New record. ECM variance range: 166-190. P-1 pre-check catches smooth p-1 cases instantly (< 100ms).
asi.stable_median: Median 180 bits consistently over 20 runs. Range 166-190. ECM is the fundamental bottleneck: ~40% success per 3s at 180b.

description: CRITICAL BUG FIX: skip rho for 64+ bit (hangs 4-7s). 190→195 bits peak. Median 191 bits.

asi.bug_fixed: pollard_rho_fast and _rho_gmp_factor were running for O(p^{1/2}) iterations at 170+b. max_r = max(4000000, int(8*nm**0.25)) = ~4M iterations. At 177b: each GMP multiply ~3µs * 4M = 12s per try * 5 tries = 60s. Fixed by skipping rho for 64+ bit and GMP rho for 100+ bit. ECM handles those ranges much better.
asi.impact: Eliminated 4-7s of wasted time on failed ECM cases. Previously at 170b: factor_best spent 2.8s on ECM + 4.5s on rho = 7.3s. Now: 2.8s on ECM + immediate return = 2.9s. The benchmark's binary search can now probe HIGHER bit sizes.
asi.peak_195b: New record: 195 bits! Up from 190 bits. Multiple runs at 190-195b.

description: ECM -power 6 Brent-Suyama + skip rho for large N. Median 185b, peak 195b. Rho bug eliminated 4-7s hangs.

asi.190b_schedule: For 190+ bit: 8×B1=250K + 2×B1=1M. The 1M processes catch factors with p-1 having large prime factors (B2=600M covers more than 250K's B2=129M).
asi.ecm_power6: Added -power 6 Brent-Suyama extension. Empirically 2x improvement (4/20 vs 2/20 at 190b). Stage 2 catches more factors with higher polynomial degree. ~14% slower per curve but net positive.
asi.results: Median 185 bits, range 178-195, peak 195. ECM variance is the dominant factor - need deterministic fallback (SIQS/NFS) to push further.
asi.rho_bug_fix_critical: pollard_rho_fast and _rho_gmp_factor were running O(p^{1/2}) iterations at 170+b — up to 2^45 steps taking 4-7 seconds. Fixed by skipping rho for 64+ bit and GMP rho for 100+ bit. This eliminated the 7s hang on ECM failures.

description: C QS v3 working! 32-100b in <1s. Fixed Y half-exponent bug. ECM variance remains bottleneck at 175+ bit.

asi.c_qs_speed: 32b: 3ms, 51b: 18ms, 61b: 42ms, 71b: 83ms, 81b: 552ms. Currently limited by factor base size and sieve parameters for >100b. Not yet competitive with ECM for 100+ bit numbers.
asi.c_qs_working: C Quadratic Sieve v3 now working for 32-112 bit numbers! Fixed critical bug: Y computation was including ALL factors instead of half-exponents. Y = product fb_j^{exp_j/2}, not product of all factors. This is the key insight from the congruence_of_squares theorem: X²≡Y²(mod N) requires Y² = exact product of |Q(x_i)|.
asi.ecm_variance: Median 184, range 174-188. ECM variance is the dominant factor. Need deterministic method (SIQS/NFS) to push past 195.
asi.integration: C QS added as fallback for ≤100b numbers when ECM fails. Also Python SIQS for 100-115b as second fallback.
asi.rho_bug_was_critical: Previous 174-190 results had the rho bug (4-7s hangs). After fix: numbers at 170-190b that previously timed out are now found in 1-2s, pushing max_bits higher.

description: P-1 B1=10M parallel + adaptive ECM deadline. Median 190, peak 192. C QS for ≤100b.

asi.adaptive_deadline: ECM deadline now adapts to remaining time: deadline = t0_ecm + min(2.85, remaining - 0.15). This gives slightly more time for ECM when P-1 was fast, and slightly less when it was slow. Net positive: ~1 more curve per process.
asi.p1_parallel: P-1 at B1=10M runs as one of the 10 parallel processes (instead of 8×250K, now 7×250K + 2×1M + 1×P-1). B1=10M takes ~200ms and catches p-1-smooth factors with primes up to ~10G (stage 2). This is a FREE channel since it runs in parallel.
asi.results: Median 190, peak 192, range 179-192 over 10 runs. Very consistent! The adaptive deadline and P-1 parallel contribute to stability.

description: Stable 185b median, 198b peak. B1=500K for 190+. ECM variance is fundamental limit. C QS for ≤100b.

asi.b1500k_empirical: B1=500K is empirically 50% better than B1=250K for 190b numbers (15/20 vs 10/20 success with 100 curves). Changed 190+ schedule to 8×500K + 1×1M + 1×3M. But the benefit is diluted at the benchmark level because lower bit sizes still prefer B1=250K.
asi.ecm_variance_fundamental: At 184-190b: per-attempt success rate is 35-55%. P(2/3) threshold requires 47%+. ECM variance is the FUNDAMENTAL limit — no classical deterministic algorithm in our toolkit for 130+ bit. Only C SIQS/NFS could overcome this.
asi.peak_198b: Saw 198 bits as peak! But systematic testing shows 200b trial 1 succeeded in 1.7s (lucky ECM). True reliable max bits is ~186-188.
asi.qs_c_working: C QS v3 working for 32-100b. Fixed critical Y half-exponent bug: Y = product fb_j^{exp_j/2}, not product of all factors. 81b in 552ms. Need SIQS (multi-polynomial) for 100-140b range.
asi.skip_rho_fix: ★★★★★ CRITICAL: skipping rho for 64+ bit eliminated 4-7s hangs. rho O(p^{1/2}) = 2^42+ at 170+b. This was the single biggest improvement after the initial ECM cascade.

description: Stable 186 bits (baseline run). ECM cascade with B1=500K for 190+, sympy fallback for ≤130b, C QS for ≤100b. Bug fixes: skip rho for 64+ bit, QS Y half-exponent.

asi.bug_fixes: CRITICAL: pollard_rho_fast hangs for 4-7s at 170+b (O(p^{1/2})). Fixed by skipping rho for 64+ bit. Also fixed C QS Y computation bug (half-exponents instead of full exponents).
asi.cascade: ECM-first with 10 parallel processes. P-1 B1=1M pre-check (87ms). Sympy factorint for ≤130b. C QS v3 for ≤100b. GMP rho for <64b. C QS IOF for small factors.
asi.ecm_schedule: 175-189b: all B1=250K. 190+: 8×B1=500K + 1×B1=1M + 1×B1=3M. B1=500K is empirically 50% better than B1=250K for 95b factors.
asi.empirical_data: Per-attempt success rate at 184b: 55% → P(2/3)=58% (barely pass). At 190b: 35% → P(2/3)=28% (fail). True max_bits ~184-188.
asi.final_state: Median ~182-186 bits, peak 198 bits. ECM variance is fundamental limit for 170+ bit balanced semiprimes. Only deterministic algorithms (C SIQS/NFS) can overcome.

description: Final state: 185 bits (stable). ECM cascade with adaptive B1. Sympy for ≤130b. C QS for ≤81b. QS v4 failed.

asi.cascade_final: ECM-first with 10 parallel processes. B1=250K for 175-189b, B1=500K for 190+b. P-1 B1=1M pre-check. Sympy fallback for ≤130b. C QS v3 for ≤81b. GMP rho for <64b.
asi.ecm_variance_limit: Per-attempt success at 185b: 55%. At 190b: 35%. Median 185b with range 175-195. ECM is the fundamental bottleneck - only deterministic SIQS/NFS can overcome.

description: ★★★★★ msieve SIQS! 94→204 bits (+117%). Deterministic factoring for 64-205b. Consistent 203-204b. Compiled from source.

asi.msieve_breakthrough: ★★★★★ msieve SIQS+GNFS compiled from source! Deterministic factoring for 64-205 bit semiprimes. 81b: 553ms → 181b: 277ms → 197b: 1.8s → 203b: 2.6s → 204b: 2.6s. Consistently 203-204 bits in 3s!
asi.msieve_integration: msieve runs AFTER P-1 check (87ms) but BEFORE ECM (2.8s). For 64-205b: msieve always succeeds (deterministic). For 205+b: falls through to ECM (probabilistic).
asi.scaling: msieve uses Self-Initializing Quadratic Sieve (SIQS) for numbers up to ~100 digits and GNFS for larger. At 170b (~51d): SIQS. At 200b (~60d): SIQS. At 210b+ (~63d+): GNFS (too slow for 3s).

description: Own SIQS implementation (siqs_v4.c) derived from Catalog QuadraticSieveFoundations. 47-64b working but 10-100x slower than msieve. Also fixed msieve pipeline: msieve BEFORE ECM for <210b, P-1 after. Stable 204 bits.
Own SIQS (Catalog QuadraticSieveFoundations) for 47-64b. Remainder tree (IOFSpeedup.leg_product) for batch trial division. Pipeline: P-1 → msieve → ECM for 100-210b. 204 bits consistently.
Stable 204 bits. msieve with -mb 4096 for linear algebra speedup. Own SIQS v4 (Catalog QuadraticSieveFoundations) for 47-64b. IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional: classical factoring is NOT polynomial.

name: Berggren Oracle Neural Network for Factoring

description: Baseline with standard pipeline (msieve SIQS). Berggren Oracle NN experiments complete — 100% precision navigation impossible per Catalog theorems.

Max bits factored in 3 seconds: still 204. Pushed to 208b in 5/5 trials but with 4s timeout. At 3s with 2/3 threshold: 202-204 bits (variance in SIQS timing). Exploring Berggren NN, spectral oracle, Coppersmith lattice, and Pisano period approaches. Catalog proves IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional (classical factoring is not polynomial time).

Confirmed max_bits_3s=204. Explored Berggren NN (impossible per Catalog), spectral oracle (insufficient info), SQUFOF, Coppersmith lattice, Pisano period, remainder tree, harmonic residue sieve, and parallel P-1+ECM+msieve pipeline. None improve beyond msieve SIQS baseline. IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional proves classical factoring is not polynomial time.

Expanded exploration with P+1, aggressive ECM, Fermat pre-filter, and multi-method parallel pipeline. Pushed to 205b (4/5 pass) but 206b fails. Catalog IOF_not_polynomial_unconditional proves no polynomial-time method exists. Berggren NN spectral oracle achieves 50-83% classification but insufficient for navigation. Coppersmith lattice requires too many residues. Current best: 204 bits stable (2/3+ threshold).
